description:
The Group-IB Threat Intelligence team identified an actor on darkforums[.]me offering a credential checker — EMailAccess Checker. The tool targets email.

The threat actor Argfilox posted a thread on darkforums[.]me on 2026-10-31:

Hidden Content
ALL DATA:
hxxps://pasted[.]pw/view.php?id=123575T

This message can also be viewed in the Darkweb section.

General information

Cracking-tools offerings put offensive capability into more hands: paid commercial tooling with its licensing defeated (cracked Cobalt Strike, nulled admin panels), services that crack a named program on order (keygens, patched license checks, deobfuscation), credential-stuffing checkers and their configs (OpenBullet, SilverBullet), and brute/scan tools aimed at network and shop panels. A cracked copy of a commercial offensive framework strips away the vendor's licensing controls and export discipline, so each such listing widens the population of actors running it; a checker or brute config names the exact login surfaces its buyers will hammer. For the vendor of the cracked product this is licence abuse that feeds real intrusions; for the services a checker targets it is advance notice of credential-stuffing traffic.

Recommendations

Preparation

  • For login surfaces named in checker/brute listings: enforce rate limits and bot detection on authentication endpoints, require MFA, and alert on credential-stuffing patterns (many accounts, few passwords, rotating proxies).
  • Monitor the underground for your product or panels in cracked-tool and checker listings; Group-IB Threat Intelligence tracks these markets and flags listings that name your software or service.
  • For software vendors: build licence checks that phone home, and watch for your product's cracked builds — their C2 and watermark defaults often identify the leaked licence.

Response

  • If your product is listed cracked, identify the leaked build or licence, revoke it, and notify customers whose watermarked copies match.
  • If your service is named as a checker target, review authentication logs for stuffing bursts and tighten the named endpoint's controls for the exposure window.
  • Request takedown of download links and report the hosting to its abuse contact.

Post-incident

  • Audit which accounts were accessed through credential stuffing and force resets on the affected population.
  • For vendors: fix the licensing weakness the crack exploits and re-key affected customers.
  • Keep monitoring for re-uploads of the same build; Group-IB can help via the Service Desk.

Disclaimer

  • Please note that the information in this report is based on statements made by alleged threat actors and should be independently verified.
  • This report was generated using artificial intelligence and may contain inaccuracies; it is advisable to double-check the provided information.
  • The recommendations above, like this notification as a whole, are generated automatically and are general in nature. Each incident is unique and should be analyzed by specialists with the appropriate experience and skills. If you would like Group-IB's specialists to review the incident and provide a more detailed description or a tailored list of recommendations, please submit a request in https://tap.group-ib.com/service_desk — our specialists will be happy to assist you.
title: An account checker (EMailAccess Checker) targeting email offered for sale
